blocks.text: Arlington's Janitorial Market in One Paragraph

Arlington is a dense, Metro-served office market directly across the Potomac from Washington, DC, with towers clustered in four submarkets: Rosslyn, Ballston, Crystal City, and Pentagon City. Janitorial pricing runs at 1.26x national benchmarks, matching the highest multipliers in our city set. The janitor median wage reference is about $20.79 per hour, and billed labor ranges from $44 to $76 per hour. Federal-adjacent high-rises near DC require top-tier security vetting and careful marble care, and DC-metro wage scales influence what vendors must pay to retain experienced crews.
Arlington Budget Table: Daily Weekday and Seven-Day Service

Arlington's government contractors, associations, and law firms often run extended hours, and towers with 24/7 operations centers commonly need seven-day coverage. The table converts the 1.26x per-visit rate to monthly totals using 4.33 weeks per month: 21.65 visits at a 0.90 frequency multiplier for weekday service and 30.33 visits at 0.87 for seven-day service.

blocks.text: Smaller tenants with lighter occupancy can drop to twice-weekly service, which on a 5,000 sq ft suite brings the monthly bill to roughly $4,910–$8,184. The per-visit minimum in Arlington lands at about $113–$170 after the multiplier, which governs pricing for very small suites in Courthouse or Clarendon walk-ups.
Rosslyn, Ballston, Crystal City, and Pentagon City Differences

items: Rosslyn: the tallest towers in the region, with marble and granite lobbies, extensive curtain wall glass, and strict landlord COI requirements. Expect premium lobby and stone-care line items.
Ballston: a mix of tech, nonprofit, and research tenants in mid-rise towers with LVT, carpet tile, and polished concrete amenity floors; pricing tends to cluster mid-band.
Crystal City: older 1970s and 1980s towers undergoing redevelopment, with significant VCT that needs periodic scrub-and-recoat and underground concourse connections that add foot traffic.
Pentagon City: retail-adjacent office with defense contractor tenants; security vetting and escort requirements are common and add labor time.

blocks.title: Marble and Stone Care Is Its Own Budget
blocks.text: Daily lobby care on marble should use a neutral pH cleaner only; acidic or ammonia products etch calcite stone. A no-rinse 1:128 neutral concentrate such as Zep's industrial floor cleaner is safe on sealed stone and terrazzo for routine mopping. Honing and polishing marble is a specialty service priced at $55–$95 nationally per labor hour, or roughly $69–$120 after Arlington's multiplier, and should be contracted separately from nightly janitorial.
VCT Restoration in Crystal City and Older Towers

Arlington's older buildings still carry thousands of square feet of VCT in corridors, mailrooms, and back-of-house areas. The amortized deep floor program runs $0.03–$0.06 per sq ft monthly nationally, or about $378–$756 per month on 10,000 sq ft in Arlington. Scrub-and-recoat cycles that use a 25%-solids, zinc-interlocked acrylic finish such as Diversey Vectra hold gloss longer under heavy scuffing, which can stretch the time between full strips. For loading docks and breakroom appliances, a biodegradable, phosphate-free degreaser like Simple Green Pro HD cuts grease without damaging stainless steel or floor finish.

blocks.text: Security Vetting, Wage Scales, and COI Requirements

Many Arlington tenants hold federal contracts, and some service contracts at federally leased buildings fall under the Service Contract Act, which sets prevailing wage and fringe benefit rates for janitors. Even commercial tenants feel the effect because vendors pay similar rates to retain staff across accounts. Security vetting typically includes criminal background checks, identity verification, and tenant badging; where federal tenants occupy floors, credentialing may take weeks, so account for transition time when changing vendors.

Class A tower COI requirements usually include $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate general liability, an umbrella of $5 million or more, auto liability, Virginia workers' compensation, and a fidelity bond. Ask for a waiver of subrogation endorsement and primary-noncontributory wording, which most Arlington landlords require.

items.name: Confirm wage obligations
items.text: Ask whether any part of your space is subject to federal prevailing wage requirements and have the vendor confirm compliance in writing.

items.name: Separate stone care from nightly service
items.text: Price marble honing and polishing as a scheduled specialty line, not an open-ended allowance.

items.name: Plan credentialing lead time
items.text: Start vendor badging two to four weeks before the contract start date.

items.name: Audit monthly
items.text: Walk the space with the vendor supervisor monthly using a written checklist tied to the scope.

faqs.q: What does office cleaning cost per month in Arlington, VA?
faqs.a: A 5,000 sq ft Arlington office pays about $567–$945 per visit. That is roughly $4,910–$8,184 per month at twice weekly, $11,048–$18,413 at five nights per week, and $14,961–$24,936 at seven days, using the 1.26x multiplier and 4.33 weeks per month.

faqs.q: Why are Arlington janitorial rates so high?
faqs.a: DC-metro wage scales, federal prevailing wage influence, security vetting requirements, and Class A tower standards such as marble care and extensive glass all push labor costs up. The result is a 1.26x multiplier over national rates.

faqs.q: Does the Service Contract Act apply to my office cleaning?
faqs.a: It applies to service contracts with federal agencies, not to private commercial leases. However, if your company holds federal contracts that include facility services, or you occupy federally leased space, check with counsel. Even when it does not apply, it influences local janitorial wages.

faqs.q: What COI language do Arlington landlords require from cleaning vendors?
faqs.a: Expect requirements for additional insured status for the owner and manager, waiver of subrogation, primary and noncontributory wording, general liability of $1 million per occurrence, an umbrella policy, Virginia workers' comp, and a fidelity bond.

faqs.q: How often should marble lobbies be professionally polished?
faqs.a: Busy Rosslyn and Crystal City lobbies usually need honing or polishing two to four times per year, with nightly neutral pH damp mopping and dust mopping in between. Price the specialty work separately so nightly janitorial bids stay comparable.
